label: Contrived and perfected the air pump
description: Hooke claimed to have perfected the air pump for Boyle, printed in 1660.

sources.quote: Our author tells us that in 1658, or the following year, he contrived and perfected the air pump for Mr Boyle, as it was printed in 1660

label: Moved to Gresham College
description: Hooke had lived at Gresham College since 1664, where the Society held its meetings.

sources.quote: Hooke had lived since 1664 in Gresham College, where the Society held its meetings

label: Published Micrographia
description: Hooke's preface to Micrographia praised Christopher Wren.

sources.quote: Hooke's praise of Christopher Wren in the preface to Micrographia, which holds Wren up as exemplary for uniting 'such a mechanical hand, and so philosophical a mind.'

label: Endowment of Cutlerian Lectureship
description: Sir John Cutler endowed a lectureship on the history of trades in 1665.

sources.quote: lectures he gave under the terms of Sir John Cutler's 1665 endowment of a lectureship on the history of trades

label: Breakdown of relationship with Oldenburg
description: Working relationship between Hooke and Henry Oldenburg broke down.

sources.quote: the problem engendered by the breakdown of the working relationship between Hooke and Henry Oldenburg in 1675

label: Published Philosophical Collections
description: Hooke published his own journal in 7 issues.

sources.quote: endeavoured to replace them with his own sporadically appearing journal, the Philosophical Collections (7 issues, 1679-82).

label: Began writing History of his own Life
description: Hooke began writing his autobiography in his diary.

sources.quote: "Saturday April the 10th 1697.  I began this day to write the History of my own Life
When he died, in March 1703, his death wasn't simply an intellectual loss to the Society

label: Newton became President of Royal Society
description: Newton rose to the Presidency eight months after Hooke's death.

sources.quote: Newton rose to pre-eminence in reputation and to the Presidency of the Royal Society... eight months after Hooke's death.
Newton was knighted in April 1705, fully two years after Hooke's death.

label: Published Posthumous Works
description: Waller published Hooke's Posthumous Works with the 'Life' prefixed.

sources.quote: Richard Waller's 'Life of Dr Robert Hooke', prefixed to his edition of Hooke's Posthumous Works (1705)

label: Waller received fresh papers
description: Waller received more of Hooke's papers in 1707.

sources.quote: we can determine that some fresh papers of Hooke's came to Waller's hands in or about 1707
